page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on KVM hypervisors. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, relying on remote block storage solutions for persistent data needs. Network throughput is capped at a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

With a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation, this server optimizes compute density for processor-bound execution rather than large in-memory footprints. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without core-contention penalties typical of shared architectures. However, the complete absence of integrated local storage means data persistence and high IOPS operations depend on network-attached volumes. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided, requiring explicit network configuration for external access.

The high vCPU core count combined with 32 Gbps baseline networking positions the ecs.c8a.24xlarge for compute-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include compute-heavy batch processing, distributed data engineering, large-scale CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, and ETL execution jobs where processing throughput is prioritized over massive memory caching or local ephemeral disk access.
